question.text: Prakriti Cat III AIF holds 1,00,000 shares of a thinly-traded SME. Daily traded volume = 25,000 shares. Current market price = INR 100. Daily price band = -2% (lower). Opportunity cost = 12% p.a. (ignore intra-day discounting for simplicity). Over how many trading days must the fund liquidate, and at approximately what un-discounted sale price on Day T+3?

explanation.text: The Logic: Days to liquidate = 1,00,000 / 25,000 = 4 days. Price series: T = 100; T+1 = 98; T+2 = 96.04; T+3 = 94.1192. Per Section 14.11.1 illustration, successive days each hit the -2% lower price band, so price multiplies by 0.98 each day. The Trap: 2 days uses wrong volume math. 5 days overshoots. 3 days stops at T+2. Cross-Exam Context: VIII (Equity Derivatives) covers market-impact models; XIX-C operationalises the concept for Cat III AIF valuation where a 2-3% haircut on illiquid SME positions is routine in the monthly NAV. Manager's Pro-Tip: For illiquid positions >1% of ADV, build a 'liquidity-discounted FMV' into your Valuation Policy. SEBI/APMI inspections question managers who mark thinly-traded SME holdings at Friday close with no volume adjustment.
